meta.storyTitle: Exclude the live store from directory searches

summary.prose: Prevent shared grep from opening the live graph data or lock file, including directory and symbolic-link root aliases. Refuse direct protected roots; route roots containing a protected descendant to the existing guarded Node walker, and retain explicitly non-following, config-independent ripgrep for other roots. Preserve public result shapes and report actual backend and exclusion semantics.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

boundary.internal: Exclude the live store from directory searches

api.name: runGrepSearch

parameters.name: opts
parameters.purpose: Existing search options and test backend seams; no new public option.

returns.meaning: Allowed matches, actual usedRipgrep flag, real truncation and explicit omissions.

errors.condition: Root resolves to the current live data or lock path.
Complete search times out or an admitted ripgrep process fails; retain existing partial-hit semantics.
Invalid pattern or unreadable/missing root, retaining existing behavior.

preconditions: Reuse symlink-aware canonical store-path resolution; compare containment using path components, never a string-prefix-only test.
Check both data and lock paths: either may resolve independently through symlinks.
postconditions: Admission order: root refusal → canonical ancestry decision → backend selection → content reads → result; filtering returned hits is insufficient.
Any root containing a protected path selects Node before rg spawn. Node reuses isLiveStoreFile immediately before each candidate content read.
Other roots may use ripgrep with --no-config and --no-follow, preventing environment config from enabling alias traversal; explicit protected file roots were already refused.
Bounded and complete modes share the same root guard. No timeout/exit failure is recast as a complete success.

Tool and analyzer are many callers → one shared grep entry → one selected backend per search. Search owns any rg child; store module retains identity-policy ownership. No new storage entities, ownership transfer, IPC payload or UI change. This conditional call flow is fully specified in prose; no ERD or companion visual is needed.

errorCases.scenario: Protected data or lock passed directly or through a symlink.
errorCases.detection: Existing symlink-aware refusal before backend admission.
errorCases.response: Typed refusal and existing failed ToolResult wrapper; never spawn rg or read contents.

errorCases.scenario: Protected file below ordinary or directory-alias root.
errorCases.detection: Canonical component-wise ancestry of either protected target, then per-file identity checks in Node.
errorCases.response: Omit protected contents before read; report Node backend and live-store exclusion rule.
errorCases.userImpact: Allowed matches still returned; no invented unreadable error for deliberate policy omission.

errorCases.scenario: Complete-mode backend fails/times out or Node root is unreadable.
errorCases.response: Preserve GrepIncompleteError with allowed partial hits or existing root error; no success from incomplete run.

edgeCases.expected: Component-safe containment does not overexclude. Lookalikes remain searchable.

edgeCases.expected: Preserve existing root error semantics in this batch; tests must not silently broaden fallback file-root behavior.
No new race-free or inode-based access policy claim; retain existing resolved-path semantics. Do not silently expand scope.

invariantsToPreserve.text: Only store owner opens current live data and lock; returning no hits after reading them is insufficient.
Preserve options/result/IPC shapes, allowed matches, bounded limits and explicit complete-mode failures.
Do not modify other file tools, registry, native lifecycle policy or release qualification.

testStrategy.testFramework: node:test with tsx on supported Node22, serial focused files under the owned harness. Typecheck/build once; do not overlap sweeps. Record baseline run 0e08a40d-5df6-4a56-94e5-99fa223b5b73: 15 pass/2 fail, no skips/cancels, including the known store leak and a distinct fake-rg 300ms startup/timing failure. Test protected read absence with instrumentation, not merely absent output. Do not raise production deadlines or blanket-skip.

migration.stateBefore: Direct roots refuse; Node descendants guard; directory ripgrep can read live data/lock. Existing fixture observes canary hits.
migration.stateAfter: Store-containing roots use guarded Node before any rg spawn; ordinary roots retain explicitly non-following rg. No persisted data or public schema change.

migrationSteps.action: Implement approved shared admission guard and focused tests; retain current store identity policy.
Run isolated source/compiled where relevant checks and typecheck, record complete counts and remaining baseline failures.
Obtain BUILD approval before completion; install/restart only under separately authorized deployment work.

migration.backwardCompat: Public options, return shape, tool IDs and analyzer API unchanged. Affected store-ancestor searches deliberately report usedRipgrep=false and Node exclusion semantics; this is visible and documented. Rolling back restores the leak and is not an acceptable production fallback.

alternativesConsidered.name: Guard backend admission using canonical store ancestry
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Use existing per-file Node enforcement when a root can contain the store; retain ripgrep for other roots.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Keep public GrepSearchOptions/SearchGrepData unchanged. Resolve root and both protected paths through the existing store path resolver. Direct protected roots refuse; directory roots containing either protected path use Node scanning with the existing identity predicate before content reads. Ripgrep elsewhere is explicitly non-following and ignores ambient config. Report actual backend and exclusions.
pros: Small shared enforcement point covers tool and analyzer bounded/complete modes.
Reuses current symlink-aware store identity and Node walker; no output-only filtering.
cons: Searches above the live store use Node and inherit its documented ignore/size rules.
Filesystem replacement between identity check and read remains an existing path-check limitation.

alternativesConsidered.name: Enumerate vetted paths for ripgrep
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Build an allowed file manifest before any content search.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Enumerate candidates using each backend's ignore semantics, validate each canonical path against protected store identity, then supply allowed paths in bounded batches to ripgrep or Node while preserving aggregate limits, errors and completeness.
pros: Can retain ripgrep content matching for store-ancestor directories.
cons: Adds traversal, argument batching and aggregate limit semantics.
Larger rewrite risks changing ignore behavior and failure reporting; still has path replacement race.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Feasible but adds complexity beyond current defect.

alternativesConsidered.name: Post-filter ripgrep matches
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Remove protected paths from returned matches after search.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Leave backend reads unchanged and apply isLiveStoreFile to parsed matches before publishing SearchGrepData.
cons: Rejected: protected files already opened, including the lock file; violates acceptance despite hiding hits.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Hiding matches cannot undo unsafe store descriptor access.

citations.quotedText: isLiveStoreFile compares resolved paths of current live data and lock.
Shared bounded/complete rg and Node search; Node contains a per-file isLiveStoreFile guard.
